title: clarify-sse-terminus-signature-and-introduce-handshake-coordinator-for-toolcalls
author: Evelyn Cho
release_notes: Fixes an ambiguous stream terminus encoding that could cause partial JSON to be emitted across reconnections; adds a small coordinator service to ensure function/tool-call frames are fenced atomically across chunk boundaries. No API surface change for end users; improves streaming robustness and compatibility with OpenAI-style SSE clients.
description:
Context and motivation: In heterogeneous client environments we observed two recurring modes of failure: 1) the stream terminator token sequence (what we call the 'terminus signature') could be split across TCP/HTTP/SSE chunks or obfuscated by heartbeat/keepalive padding, producing truncated JSON objects on reconnect; 2) tool/function-call handoffs that rely on implicit event ordering could race with reassembly heuristics and produce mis-ordered function-call metadata. Users hit this in a high-throughput private deployment and during an incident (SUP-5412) where third-party SSE proxies coalesced keepalives.

Goals: (a) unambiguously detect and recover a stream-level terminus even when split across chunks; (b) guarantee an atomic fence for tool/function-call frames so that downstream consumers never see a partial tool metadata payload without its accompanying content; (c) remain backward compatible with existing OpenAI-compat clients and proxies.

Changes in this PR: - Introduce a canonical "terminus signature" matcher that works across chunk boundaries and tolerates interleaved keepalive heartbeats; implemented in sse/parser.rs and exposed to the compatibility layer. The matcher uses a tiny rolling window scan and a short checksum to avoid false positives on long-lived streams. - Add a lightweight handshake coordinator (handshake_coordinator.go) co-located in the compat layer that sequences tool-call start/end fences and ensures the emitter flushes a terminus-adjacent checkpoint before yielding control to a tool runner. The coordinator exposes a small async API: BeginFence/EndFence but this remains internal to the compatibility layer (no public SDK change). - Update the Python and Go streaming compat adapters to use the coordinator: compatibility/stream_compat_layer.py and sse/handshake_coordinator.go. - Add deterministic end-to-end tests that simulate chunk splits, keepalives, and proxy coalescing (tests/test_stream_handshake.py + tests/fixtures/*). - Documentation: docs/streaming_behavior.md explains the terminus semantics and recommended proxy settings.

Implementation notes & rationale: - We intentionally avoided adding extra framing bytes to the wire to remain compatible with strict SSE proxies and clients. Instead the terminus signature is chosen to be a short, low-collision sequence plus a 8-bit rolling checksum when emitted by Redwood’s runtime. Clients that do not emit the checksum still interoperate: the parser will fallback to a conservative reassembly path with a small additional latency penalty. - The handshake coordinator is a best-effort sequencer: it prevents the compat layer from yielding a function/tool-call event until the emitter confirms the terminus checkpoint is durable. This prevents other consumers (e.g., proxy reconnections) from observing half-committed tool metadata. - Performance: microbenchmarks show an average 0.6ms median per-call overhead in the compat layer for typical 128-token responses (see bench notes in the PR commit).

Checklist: - [x] Parser roll-window matcher implemented and unit-tested - [x] Handshake coordinator implemented with Go and Python adapters - [x] Integration tests simulate proxy chunking and heartbeat interleaving - [x] Docs updated with guidance for proxies and SDKs - [x] Verified fallbacks for older clients - [x] Benchmarks added

Summary of commits: - 8c1f4a1: sse/parser.rs: add terminus signature rolling matcher and checksum fallback - 9b2d3f7: handshake_coordinator.go: implement BeginFence/EndFence + in-memory checkpoint - e4a7b2c: compatibility/stream_compat_layer.py: wire coordinator into streamer loop and add logging - f1d9c88: tests/test_stream_handshake.py: new integration harness w/ proxy simulation - a5b6c3d: docs/streaming_behavior.md: document terminus semantics and proxy guidance

Changed files (high level): - sse/parser.rs: new matcher + unit tests (parser/terminus_tests.rs) - sse/handshake_coordinator.go: coordinator and small in-memory checkpoint - compatibility/stream_compat_layer.py: adapters to call BeginFence/EndFence and emit checksum header - tests/test_stream_handshake.py and tests/fixtures/: end-to-end simulations - docs/streaming_behavior.md: guidance and migration notes

Review conversation (selected threads): - Devon Kim (reviewer): "Can we reduce the rolling checksum width? 8-bit seems sufficient but may still cause a tiny collision window on long-lived multiplexed streams." Author reply (Evelyn): "We started with 16-bit and iterated down; 8-bit gives acceptable safety vs. backwards compatibility. Added a comment and a small metric (terminus_checksum_collisions_count) so we can revisit if necessary." - Samir Patel (reviewer): "The coordinator feels like another point of coupling between runtime and compat. How will this behave under load and when the emitter is overloaded?" Author reply: "Coordinator is best-effort: timeouts are applied and we fallback to a conservative reassembly path emitting a recovery marker. Added integration test that simulates emitter overload (test simulates a stall and verifies the recovery marker is emitted)." - Arianna Park (approver): "Looks good — the tests exercise edge cases and the docs are clear. One nit: expand the migration note to call out nginx proxy config that caused the incident." Author reply: "Added nginx sample config and an ops note to docs/streaming_behavior.md per Arianna's suggestion."

CI and gating: - Initial CI run: build and unit tests passed; integration tests failed due to flaky proxy simulator on mac runners. - Second run after test harness fix: all checks passed (build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, lint: pass).

Merge notes: - Merge method: squash and merge - Merge commit: 7b3d2c9 - Post-merge follow-ups: ENG-2198 to instrument terminus_checksum_collisions_count in production dashboards; a small follow-up PR will add a graceful degradation metric and opt-in debug logging for private deployments.

Impact: This PR does not change the public API; it reduces incidence of partial JSON emissions and misordered tool/function-call events in the wild. Operators should review docs/streaming_behavior.md and evaluate proxy settings; recommend enabling the small checksum header in environments where proxies are known to coalesce SSE frames.
